assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, gave a measurement tool with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18. That is a new regime for time and frequency metrology, with uses in relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. It is an instrument-driven advance of the kind I value: patient control of systematics that opens a new window.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and made the first demonstrations. Jun Ye took the clocks to the highest accuracy and showed many-body and geodetic applications. Two laureates is a clean configuration. Related ion-clock and frequency-comb contributions are largely recognised by the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
assessment.maturity: Several independent groups (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) agree at the 1e-18 level and international comparisons are routine. A redefinition of the second is under discussion. The recognition would be timely, not premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes may make some members see it as incremental.
Whether the committee wants to credit the magic-wavelength concept separately from the accuracy record is unresolved.
Details of early priority between groups are from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and later the TXS 0506+056 blazar association, opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. A cubic-kilometre instrument in Antarctic ice is a major detector achievement and a new observational window, squarely in my field.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the cubic-kilometre concept after AMANDA, and Karle built central parts of the detector and the analysis. A collaboration of several hundred people and the contributions of Spiering and others from the AMANDA era make a three-person limit hard. The credit is more contested than for a single-inventor result.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established at high significance and cross-checked in several channels, including through-going muons and cascades. The Galactic plane and NGC 1068 results strengthen the case. The sources of most events remain unknown, but the discovery of the flux itself is solid.
uncertainties: Individual attribution within a large collaboration is contested.
The astrophysical source population is largely unidentified, so some will call the interpretation incomplete.
Whether the correct credit includes Spiering or others is uncertain, and I am working from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in electron lenses overcame the Scherzer limit and made routine sub-angstrom imaging in TEM and STEM possible. It had a large downstream effect on materials physics, chemistry and nanoscience. This is a textbook instrument breakthrough: the idea, the engineering and the demonstration were all required.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theory of multipole correctors, and Haider and Urban built and demonstrated the first working TEM corrector. Krivanek, who built the STEM corrector, is not in the credited list. The three credited names are the natural trio for the TEM route, but the STEM contribution is an unresolved credit question.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently for decades. Thousands of instruments operate worldwide, and the work has already received major prizes. The 1986 Nobel recognised the electron microscope itself, so this is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Krivanek's STEM corrector and its omission from the credited names create an allocation problem.
Some members may see this as chemistry or instrumentation rather than physics.
Priority details are from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays gave evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries, using millisecond pulsars as a galaxy-sized detector. It is original and beautiful instrumentation: timing precision at the 100 ns level sustained over decades.
assessment.attribution: Manchester led the Parkes PTA, Kramer led European PTA work, and McLaughlin is prominent in NANOGrav, while Hobbs, Foster, Jenet and others did key early work. Credit is spread across at least three regional collaborations, and the three names given are not clearly the decisive ones. The attribution is hard.
assessment.maturity: Evidence from NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA and CPTA appeared together in 2023 with a Hellings-Downs correlation at roughly 2-4 sigma. The combined IPTA analysis was not complete when I last knew. The source of the signal is not settled. Promising but possibly premature.
uncertainties: The significance is below 5 sigma as far as I know, and the origin (black-hole binaries versus new physics) is unsettled.
Credit is spread over multiple PTAs and individuals, so the supplied trio may be unfair.
Whether the evidence has matured enough by 2026 is unknown to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* gave direct evidence of supermassive black-hole shadows and tested general relativity in the strong field. This is a technically remarkable VLBI achievement, with calibration and imaging challenges I respect.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the EHT, and Moran was a VLBI pioneer. The collaboration is over 300 people and the imaging work involved many leaders. Attribution to three people is fair in part but contestable.
assessment.maturity: The images have been followed by additional epochs and polarisation results, and independent imaging pipelines agree, though the data come from a single array. The black-hole prizes of 2017 and 2020 came earlier, so this builds on them. Reasonably mature, but possibly early.
uncertainties: The data come from one collaboration, so independent confirmation is limited.
Falcke's role versus others in the concept is contested.
Some will argue the physics was already honoured in 2020.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking and is one of the central experimental results in particle physics. The detector design and calibration took decades of work.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize went to Englert and Higgs for the theory, and the experimental side was left out. Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee led ATLAS and CMS, Evans built the LHC and Della Negra was a founding figure of CMS. Choosing three from five is the hardest part, and the statutes make collaboration prizes difficult.
assessment.maturity: Both experiments confirmed it independently, with many follow-up coupling measurements and a mass near 125 GeV. The discovery is fully mature. Recognition is arguably overdue, but the committee already acted in 2013.
uncertainties: The three-person limit versus a team effort of thousands.
The committee may feel the 2013 prize closed the matter.
Allocation among Gianotti, Jenni, Virdee, Della Negra and Evans is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Laser-plasma wakefield acceleration offers gradients far above those of conventional RF structures. The Tajima-Dawson idea was followed by the 2004 monoenergetic electron beams and later GeV beams. It is a new accelerator technique with the prospect of compact sources.
assessment.attribution: Tajima proposed the concept with Dawson, who died in 2001 and is not credited. Malka, Leemans and others delivered the 2004 breakthroughs, which involved several groups. The 2018 prize recognised chirped-pulse amplification, which the idea relies on, so the credit boundaries are tricky.
assessment.maturity: Laboratory results are reproducible across groups, and free-electron laser lasing with plasma beams has been shown. Beam quality, repetition rate and stability are not yet at the level for wide application. The impact is still prospective.
uncertainties: Dawson's absence limits a fair attribution of the original concept.
Beam quality and reliability are not yet at the level for broad use.
The choice of Malka and Leemans among the 2004 groups is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Lorimer burst in 2007 revealed fast radio bursts, a new class of millisecond extragalactic radio transients. Later localisations to host galaxies and the 2020 Galactic magnetar burst made them a major topic in astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Lorimer, McLaughlin and Bailes made the discovery from archival Parkes data, and the 2013 Thornton et al. work confirmed the population. CHIME and ASKAP localisations involve other people. The discovery credit is relatively clear, but later developments involve others.
assessment.maturity: Thousands of events are known and the extragalactic origin is confirmed. The physical mechanism and progenitors are still debated, so the interpretation is not stable. Recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: The physical origin is not yet settled.
The roles of Thornton, Shannon, Bannister and the CHIME team are not covered by the credited names.
Parkes archival discovery details are from memory.
